predictions.source_summary: The YouTube ID comes from the data-youtube attribute of an HTML element. The youtubeParams string comes from the data-ytparams attribute, which may contain user-provided parameters.
predictions.sink_summary: The constructed iframe HTML is assigned to elem.innerHTML, which directly affects the DOM and can lead to XSS if user-controllable parameters are not properly sanitized.
predictions.guard_summary: There is minimal sanitization. The code checks if youtubeParams starts with '&' and prepends it if not, but does not validate or sanitize the content of youtubeParams for security-sensitive contexts.
predictions.risk_pattern: User-provided data from HTML attributes (data-youtube, data-ytparams) flows directly into DOM manipulation via innerHTML without sufficient sanitization or escaping, creating a potential XSS vulnerability when iframe parameters are user-controllable.
predictions.context_summary: The function embedYoutubeIframe is triggered by a lazyload event. It extracts YouTube ID and parameters from HTML data attributes, constructs an iframe URL with these values, and injects it into the DOM via innerHTML.
